problem: The example asks the student to make the screen show 'Hello, Chennai', then counts three edited files including MainActivity.java. No Java edit is needed: the template already calls setContentView(R.layout.activity_main), and the TextView gets its text from @string/greeting in the layout. Step 3 itself admits findViewById is only for changing text at run time, so it contradicts the answer.
fix: Only two files are edited: res/values/strings.xml (add the greeting string) and res/layout/activity_main.xml (add TextView with id text1 and text @string/greeting). MainActivity.java is left unchanged; its existing setContentView already inflates activity_main. Answer (b): two files.

problem: Saying MainActivity 'extends Activity' does not match what Android Studio generates. The Empty Activity template produces a class extending AppCompatActivity (an androidx subclass of Activity); a plain Activity also forces a non-AppCompat theme.
fix: Write that the template's MainActivity extends AppCompatActivity, which itself extends Activity; onCreate is overridden in both cases and setContentView behaves the same.

problem: 'A crash on launch usually points to the manifest or a missing layout name' is misleading. A missing or misspelled layout resource fails the build (no R.layout constant), so it cannot cause a launch crash. Runtime crashes on launch typically come from an undeclared activity or a findViewById returning null (wrong id, or called after a changed layout).
fix: 'A crash on launch usually points to the manifest (activity not declared, wrong theme) or to findViewById returning null because the id is missing from the inflated layout. A missing layout file stops the build instead.'

problem: "Writing import com.example.hello.R by hand" is described as a mistake, but R for this module lives in com.example.hello, the same package as MainActivity, so such an import is redundant, not wrong. The real mistake students make is importing android.R by accident.
fix: Say: no import of R is needed because R sits in the app's own package; the harmful one is import android.R, and a red R almost always means a resource error somewhere, not a missing import.

problem: Students using a current Android Studio see MainActivity.kt and build.gradle.kts by default, while the chapter speaks only of Java files and build.gradle. Nothing in the chapter tells them how to get the Java/XML project the chapter assumes.
fix: Add one sentence: in the New Project wizard choose the Java language (and Groovy DSL if offered), so the module file is build.gradle and the activity is MainActivity.java; Kotlin projects follow the same anatomy with .kt files and build.gradle.kts.
